scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Your phone shows a blue dot, right on your street, using satellites twenty thousand kilometres away. But how?

scenes.name: sats
scenes.text: About thirty GPS satellites circle Earth. Each carries atomic clocks, and keeps broadcasting its position and the exact time.

scenes.name: time
scenes.text: Your phone only listens. It compares when each signal was sent with when it arrived. A gap of about seven hundredths of a second.

scenes.name: dist
scenes.text: Radio travels at the speed of light, so that time, multiplied by the speed, gives your distance from that satellite.

scenes.name: tri
scenes.text: One distance puts you somewhere on a giant sphere. Three spheres cross at one point. A fourth satellite fixes your phone's clock error.

scenes.name: fast
scenes.text: Phones speed this up with help from mobile networks, and use other systems too, like India's NavIC.

scenes.name: acc
scenes.text: In open sky, that's usually within about five metres. Tall buildings bounce signals, and make it worse.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Clocks, timing, distance, spheres. Your dot, from space. Follow for more on how things really work.
